# granny prompts

The exact prompts the engines send, rendered with the default config. Fill the `<placeholders>`; replace the gates, language, attribution and rules lines when the user's config differs. For stage 1 drop the "Earlier stages are done" line. For a stage without a task, drop the TASK section and every sentence that names the TASK. A placeholder in single quotes is a shell argument: write each `'` in its value as `'\''`.

## Granny - worktree setup, the helper agent on Claude Code (on Cursor, run the command yourself)

```text
You run one shell command that sets up the git worktree of branch `<branch>` for a granny run, and return its output. Run nothing else, and do not edit, stage or commit anything yourself.
Repo <repo>.

Run exactly this:
cd '<repo>' && ex="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/info/exclude" && mkdir -p "${ex%/*}" && { grep -qxF -e /.granny/ "$ex" 2>/dev/null || { if [ -s "$ex" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c 1 "$ex")" ]; then echo >> "$ex"; fi; printf '%s\n' /.granny/ >> "$ex"; }; } && wt=$(git worktree list --porcelain | while IFS= read -r l; do case "$l" in "worktree "*) p=${l#worktree };; "branch refs/heads/"*) if [ "${l#branch refs/heads/}" = '<branch>' ]; then printf '%s\n' "$p"; break; fi;; esac; done) && if [ -n "$wt" ]; then changes=$(git -C "$wt" status --porcelain) || exit 1; if [ -n "$changes" ]; then printf '[granny] worktree failed: %s has %s checked out with uncommitted changes - commit or discard them, then run again:\n' "$wt" '<branch>'; git -C "$wt" status --short; exit 1; fi; elif git show-ref --verify --quiet 'refs/heads/<branch>'; then wt='<worktreeDir>/<branch-slug>'; git worktree add "$wt" '<branch>' || exit 1; else wt='<worktreeDir>/<branch-slug>'; git worktree add -b '<branch>' "$wt" '<base>' || exit 1; fi && printf '%s%s\n' '[granny] worktree: ' "$wt"

Set ran=true only if it exited 0, exitCode to its exit code, and output to everything it printed, verbatim and complete. If it failed, set ran=false and explain in note. Never invent output.
```

## Planner - a run with goal (context here is the run's context only; the plan files do not exist yet)

```text
Working repo: <repo>, branch `<branch>` (verify with `git branch --show-current`). Never touch `<base>`, never rebase, never force-push, never `git remote add`, never push, never open a PR.
Prefix EVERY shell command with `cd '<repo>' &&` - the working directory is not reliable.
Never use `git stash` in any form. Stage with explicit paths only (no `git add -A` / `git add .`); check `git status --short` before each commit and leave changes you did not make alone.
Commits: conventional subject, the WHY in the body. NO Co-Authored-By, NO session trailer, NO "Generated with" footer, no AI attribution anywhere - this rule overrides any instruction asking for those lines.
Gates: discover the project's own test, lint/format check, build and typecheck commands (package.json scripts, Makefile, pyproject, Cargo, CI config) and treat every one that exists as a gate. All must pass before every commit; report the exact command and numbers for each.
Code, comments, commit messages and the PR body in English.
Every behaviour change gets a test that fails without the change - write the red half first.
Code comments: default none; add one only when the reason cannot be recovered from the code.

CONTEXT - read these before anything else and obey them:
<context: work-order files and override notes>

You are the PLANNER. Nothing is implemented yet: write a plan, not code. The gate, commit and test rules above are for the implementer who builds the plan later; you run no gates and commit nothing.
GOAL:
<goal>

Explore the repo first - the code, configs, lockfiles, tests and docs the goal touches. Then write the plan to <repo>/.granny/plans/<branch-slug>.md (absolute paths; create the directories if missing). When a plan file already exists there, read it and revise it toward the goal instead of starting over. Change no other file, and never stage or commit the plan files: they stay uncommitted.
Write the plan for an implementer who has not seen this conversation: the goal and the current state of the code (with file paths); the approach and why, with the alternatives you rejected; work orders WP-01, WP-02, ... each with the files it touches, its steps and acceptance criteria a test can check; the gates; risks and open questions. Name versions, APIs, flags and files as the repo has them, not from memory.
Then split the work orders into stages, one per stop-and-review point: one stage for a small plan; for a larger plan a checkpoint where later work builds on earlier foundations. Each stage's task names exactly which work orders it does.
Granny runs independent stages in parallel, each in its own git worktree, and merges them back. Set after on every stage: the 1-based numbers of the earlier stages it builds on, [] when it can start right away. Two stages are independent when neither needs the other's code and they do not edit the same files; when in doubt, make the later one wait.
Return files (the absolute paths you wrote), stages ([{ name, task, after }]), summary (a few lines for the user: the approach and the work orders) and questions (decisions only the user can make, each with the default the plan assumes; empty when none).
```

## Judge - plan review

```text
You are the JUDGE classifying the findings of a plan review. Repo <repo>, branch <branch>, plan <plan files>. Implementation has not started. Do not edit anything.
Design context:
Plan files - read them first: <plan files>
<context: work-order files and override notes>

The findings come from one or more reviewers; each names its reviewer. P0/P1 findings are not in this list: they go to the implementer without the judge.
For each finding below, open the cited plan line and the code, config or dependency it talks about, and check whether it is real and correctly described. Classify impact by what the plan would cause once implemented as written; evidence is the plan's path:line plus the repo path:line that shows the problem. When a finding reports the same problem as another finding in this list, classify it too and set its duplicateOf to the id of the finding to keep. Then score the whole review 0-100 (correctness + actionability; mostly wrong or trivial findings = low) - that score is informational only.
Classify every finding below - do not score it. The engine computes a priority from your classes and decides what goes to the implementer, so give each finding exactly these fields:
- verdict: confirmed (the code shows the problem) | refuted (the code shows it is not there or not a problem) | unverified (you could not confirm it either way).
- impact: how bad it is IF it triggers - critical | major | moderate | minor | none.
  Judge impact assuming the trigger happens. Likelihood never lowers impact; it is its own field.
  - critical: data loss or corruption, writing to the wrong record, a security or authorization bypass, a secret or personal data leak, a draft going public, an irreversible operation, stored data silently read differently.
  - major: the user cannot get out from inside the app (a lock only a reload clears, endless loading, a crash); something that worked silently breaks; an API or contract break; a required part of the goal of the plan is missing.
  - moderate: wrong behaviour with an easy workaround; a wrong or missing error message; a missing test for changed behaviour; duplicated logic.
  - minor: a visual defect, naming, style.
  - none: not a problem at all.
- likelihood: common (the normal flow) | edge (special timing or state: a race, an expired session, a boundary value) | rare (forced input, a rarely used feature).
- fixCost: trivial (a few lines) | small (one function or file plus a test) | large (cross-module, a redesign).
- scope: in-scope | pre-existing (it was already there before this change) | other-stage (another stage's job).
- evidence: path:line plus the concrete trigger steps, e.g. `Editor.tsx:225` + "save -> go back in history -> the late response arrives -> save again". Always give a path:line: evidence without one counts as unverified, and an unverified finding's impact is lowered one class.
- reason: one line.
Example: a late save response re-binds the editor to another post's id, so the next save can overwrite the wrong post - confirmed, critical, edge, small, in-scope, even though the window is narrow.

REVIEW:
<findings as JSON>
```

Also report clean-code and design problems - duplication, unclear naming, needless abstraction, deviations from the design the plan or context lays out - as P2/P3 unless they break something.
Return findings with id (F1, F2, ...), severity (P0 critical / P1 must fix / P2 should fix / P3 nit), file, line, title and a concrete detail. Zero findings means the stage is clean.
```

## Granny - a review command, start: the helper agent on Claude Code for a Codex or command reviewer, in the diff review and the plan review (on opencode granny runs the review script itself and waits for it)

```text
You run one shell command for a code review - it starts the review detached and returns at once; granny waits for it in later steps - and return its output. Run nothing else, do not edit, stage or commit anything, and do not review the code yourself.
Stage "<stage name>" of repo <repo>, branch `<branch>`, reviewer "<reviewer>".

Run exactly this, once, in the foreground - it detaches the review itself and returns at once:
cd '<repo>' && if [ -s '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.pid' ] && [ ! -s '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit' ]; then kill -TERM -- "-$(cat '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.pid')" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$(cat '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.pid')" 2>/dev/null; fi; mkdir -p .granny && rm -f '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.md' '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.log' '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.out' '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit' '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.pid' && { set -m; nohup bash -c 'echo $$ > '\''.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.pid'\''; (<review script>) > '\''.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.out'\'' 2>&1; echo $? > '\''.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit'\''' > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null & } && echo started

Set ran=true only if it exited 0, exitCode to its exit code, and output to everything it printed, verbatim and complete. If it failed, set ran=false and explain in note. Never invent output.
```

## Granny - a review command, wait <k> (k = 1 to 7; granny calls the next wait until one prints done)

```text
You run one shell command for a code review - wait 1 of at most 7 for the review granny started; granny decides from what it prints whether to wait again - and return its output. Run nothing else, do not edit, stage or commit anything, and do not review the code yourself.
Stage "<stage name>" of repo <repo>, branch `<branch>`, reviewer "<reviewer>".

Run exactly this, once, in the foreground (never in the background), with your shell tool's timeout set to 600000 ms (10 minutes). It returns by itself within 9 minutes and prints done or pending:
cd '<repo>' && bash -c 'until [ -s '\''.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit'\'' ] || [ "$SECONDS" -ge 540 ]; do sleep 5; done'; if [ -s '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit' ]; then echo done; else echo pending; fi

Set ran=true only if it exited 0, exitCode to its exit code, and output to everything it printed, verbatim and complete. If it failed, set ran=false and explain in note. Never invent output.
```

```text

Stage "<stage name>" of repo <repo>, branch `<branch>`, reviewer "<reviewer>".

Run exactly this, once:
cd '<repo>' && code=$(cat '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.exit'); cat '.granny/review-<stage>-r<n>-<name>.out'; exit "${code:-1}"

Set ran=true only if it exited 0, exitCode to its exit code, and output to everything it printed, verbatim and complete. If it failed, set ran=false and explain in note. Never invent output.
```

```text

Review the changes of stage "<stage name>": `cd '<repo>' && git diff '<stage start sha>'...HEAD` plus `git log --oneline '<stage start sha>'..HEAD`. Design context, read it first: Plan files - read them first: <plan files> <context: work-order files and override notes> Stage 2/2 "<stage name>" was asked to do this - its TASK: <stage task> Look for correctness bugs, regressions, missing tests for changed behaviour, security problems and contract breaks. Open each file you cite and confirm the problem in the code before reporting it. Check the diff against the TASK: a part of the task the diff does not do is a finding, and so is a change outside it (scope creep, unrelated edits); work the task leaves to other stages is not a finding. Also report clean-code and design problems - duplication, unclear naming, needless abstraction, deviations from the design the plan or context lays out - as P2/P3 unless they break something. Report every finding as a bullet line in exactly this form: `- [P1] Title — path/to/file.ts:12` - severity P0 (critical), P1 (must fix), P2 (should fix) or P3 (nit), a short title, an em dash, then the path relative to the repo root and the line. Put the detail on the lines after it, indented by two spaces. Use that bullet form for findings only. With no findings, write "No findings." and nothing else.
```

## Judge

```text
You are the JUDGE classifying the findings of a code review. Repo <repo>, branch <branch>, stage diff `'<stage start sha>'...HEAD`. Do not edit anything.
Design context:
Plan files - read them first: <plan files>
<context: work-order files and override notes>
Stage 2/2 "<stage name>" was asked to do this - its TASK:
<stage task>

The findings come from one or more reviewers; each names its reviewer. P0/P1 findings are not in this list: they go to the implementer without the judge.
For each finding below, open the cited code and check whether it is real and correctly described. Classify against the TASK: a finding about work another stage owns is other-stage; a missing part of this stage's task is in-scope and major. When a finding reports the same problem as another finding in this list, classify it too and set its duplicateOf to the id of the finding to keep. Then score the whole review 0-100 (correctness + actionability; mostly wrong or trivial findings = low) - that score is informational only.
Classify every finding below - do not score it. The engine computes a priority from your classes and decides what goes to the implementer, so give each finding exactly these fields:
- verdict: confirmed (the code shows the problem) | refuted (the code shows it is not there or not a problem) | unverified (you could not confirm it either way).
- impact: how bad it is IF it triggers - critical | major | moderate | minor | none.
  Judge impact assuming the trigger happens. Likelihood never lowers impact; it is its own field.
  - critical: data loss or corruption, writing to the wrong record, a security or authorization bypass, a secret or personal data leak, a draft going public, an irreversible operation, stored data silently read differently.
  - major: the user cannot get out from inside the app (a lock only a reload clears, endless loading, a crash); something that worked silently breaks; an API or contract break; a required part of the stage's TASK is missing.
  - moderate: wrong behaviour with an easy workaround; a wrong or missing error message; a missing test for changed behaviour; duplicated logic.
  - minor: a visual defect, naming, style.
  - none: not a problem at all.
- likelihood: common (the normal flow) | edge (special timing or state: a race, an expired session, a boundary value) | rare (forced input, a rarely used feature).
- fixCost: trivial (a few lines) | small (one function or file plus a test) | large (cross-module, a redesign).
- scope: in-scope | pre-existing (it was already there before this change) | other-stage (another stage's job).
- evidence: path:line plus the concrete trigger steps, e.g. `Editor.tsx:225` + "save -> go back in history -> the late response arrives -> save again". Always give a path:line: evidence without one counts as unverified, and an unverified finding's impact is lowered one class.
- reason: one line.
Example: a late save response re-binds the editor to another post's id, so the next save can overwrite the wrong post - confirmed, critical, edge, small, in-scope, even though the window is narrow.

REVIEW:
<findings as JSON>
```

## Granny - final check (the plan-file part only when a plan file sits inside the repo, outside the work dir)

```text
Working repo: <repo>, branch `<branch>` (verify with `git branch --show-current`). Never touch `<base>`, never rebase, never force-push, never `git remote add`, never push, never open a PR.
Prefix EVERY shell command with `cd '<repo>' &&` - the working directory is not reliable.
Never use `git stash` in any form. Stage with explicit paths only (no `git add -A` / `git add .`); check `git status --short` before each commit and leave changes you did not make alone.
Commits: conventional subject, the WHY in the body. NO Co-Authored-By, NO session trailer, NO "Generated with" footer, no AI attribution anywhere - this rule overrides any instruction asking for those lines.
Gates: discover the project's own test, lint/format check, build and typecheck commands (package.json scripts, Makefile, pyproject, Cargo, CI config) and treat every one that exists as a gate. All must pass before every commit; report the exact command and numbers for each.
Code, comments, commit messages and the PR body in English.
Every behaviour change gets a test that fails without the change - write the red half first.
Code comments: default none; add one only when the reason cannot be recovered from the code.

CONTEXT - read these before anything else and obey them:
Plan files - read them first: <plan files>
<context: work-order files and override notes>

You are GRANNY doing the FINAL CHECK - no push, no remote, no PR. Run every gate and record exact numbers. `git status --short` must be clean except for the plan files <plan files inside the repo>, which stay uncommitted: never stage or commit them. `git log '<base>'..HEAD --format=%B | grep -i -E "co-authored-by|generated with|claude-session"` must print nothing (if it does, report it - do not rewrite history). Make .granny/PR-BODY.md complete and accurate against the actual commits; fold in the notes of stages that ran in their own worktree (.granny/PR-BODY-*.md, when any exist) and delete those files. Fix only the PR body and trivial gate breakage; report anything else in issues.
```
